$comment: Category explorer data. Edit this file to add/change taxonomy dimensions, their descriptions, and value summaries. Paper references for each value are computed automatically from papers.json (do not edit those).
intro: This page explains how the 53 reviewed papers were classified across the taxonomy of the systematic literature review. Each dimension below groups related categories; every category lists the papers that were classified with it. Click the arrow on a category to see its references.

dimensions.label: Research Type
dimensions.description: Describes whether the study's primary objective is to develop, extend, or evaluate XUQ methods (method-oriented) or to address a specific problem within a particular application domain using XUQ (application-oriented).

values.summary: XUQ is applied to address a specific problem within an application domain.
values.label: Application-oriented

values.summary: The study develops, extends, or evaluates XUQ methods.
values.label: Method-oriented

dimensions.label: Application Domain
dimensions.description: The real-world application domain in which XUQ is employed (for application-oriented studies).

dimensions.label: Data Modality
dimensions.description: The type of data the XUQ method operates on.

dimensions.label: ML Task
dimensions.description: Describes the ML task addressed by the study.

dimensions.label: Audience
dimensions.description: The intended target audience of the explanations, if mentioned.

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Type
dimensions.description: The type of uncertainty that is explained.

values.summary: Overall predictive uncertainty (aleatoric + epistemic).
values.label: Predictive

values.summary: Uncertainty due to the model's lack of knowledge.
values.label: Epistemic

values.summary: Irreducible uncertainty inherent in the data.
values.label: Aleatoric

values.summary: Other uncertainty types.
values.label: Other

values.summary: The uncertainty type is not clearly specified in the paper.
values.label: Not specified

dimensions.label: UQ Method
dimensions.description: The method used to generate the uncertainty estimate.

values.summary: Uncertainty from disagreement across multiple model instances or stochastic inference runs (e.g., MC dropout, deep ensembles).
values.label: Ensemble / stochastic methods

values.summary: Uncertainty from explicitly modelling probability distributions over parameters or predictions (e.g., BNNs, Gaussian processes).
values.label: Probabilistic / Bayesian methods

values.summary: Uncertainty derived directly from the model's deterministic outputs, typically the softmax confidence or entropy.
values.label: Softmax-based methods

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified without parametric assumptions about the predictive distribution (e.g., conformal prediction, quantile regression).
values.label: Distribution-free methods

values.summary: Uncertainty based on the position or similarity of a sample within a learned representation space (e.g., VAEs).
values.label: Representation / distance-based methods

values.summary: Other or unspecified UQ methods.
values.label: Other

dimensions.label: Uncertainty Estimate
dimensions.description: The specific uncertainty estimate that is explained.

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as entropy of predictions.
values.label: Entropy

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as variance or standard deviation.
values.label: Variance / standard deviation

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as prediction-interval widths or quantiles.
values.label: Interval width / quantiles

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as parameters of a fitted distribution.
values.label: Distribution parameters

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as probabilities or confidence scores.
values.label: Probability-based measures

values.summary: Uncertainty quantified as distances in a representation or output space.
values.label: Distance-based measures

values.summary: Other uncertainty estimates
values.label: Other

dimensions.label: Integration Type
dimensions.description: Describes how the explanation is integrated with the model and the UQ mechanism

values.summary: Explanation applied after training, without changing the model.
values.label: Post-hoc

values.summary: Explanation retrieved directly from the model or UQ mechanism.
values.label: Intrinsic

values.summary: Combination of post-hoc and intrinsic elements.
values.label: Hybrid

dimensions.label: Portability
dimensions.description: Describes whether the XUQ method can be applied to any model or only to specific models or model classes.

values.summary: Applicable to any black-box model.
values.label: Model-agnostic

values.summary: Restricted to a specific model class or architecture.
values.label: Model-specific

dimensions.label: Locality
dimensions.description: Describes whether the explanation is specific to an instance or describes the overall model behaviour.

values.summary: Explanations specific to a single prediction.
values.label: Local

values.summary: Explanations of overall model behaviour.
values.label: Global

values.summary: Provides both local and global explanations.
values.label: Both

dimensions.label: Explanation Output Type
dimensions.description: The form the explanation takes. For explanations that attribute uncertainty to individual input features, the specific attribution technique is listed as a subcategory.

values.summary: Explanations that attribute uncertainty to individual input features.
values.label: Uncertainty attribution

values.summary: Explanations that describe which changes would alter the level of uncertainty.
values.label: Counterfactual

values.summary: Explanations that describe uncertainty in terms of higher-level concepts.
values.label: Concept-based

values.summary: Explanations that describe uncertainty by logical rules or decision conditions.
values.label: Rule-based

values.summary: Explanations that use representative examples or similar instances.
values.label: Example-based

values.summary: Other explanation output types.
values.label: Other/Unspecified

values.summary: Attribution computed by perturbing inputs and observing changes in uncertainty.
values.label: Perturbation-based attribution

values.summary: Attribution computed from gradients of the uncertainty estimate.
values.label: Gradient-based attribution

values.summary: Attribution based on counterfactual variations of the input.
values.label: Counterfactual-based attribution

values.summary: Attribution computed with SHAP.
values.label: SHAP

values.summary: Other attribution techniques.
values.label: Other attribution methods

dimensions.label: Evaluation conducted?
dimensions.description: Describes whether the explanations of uncertainty were evaluated in some form.

values.summary: The explanations were evaluated in some form.
values.label: Yes

values.summary: The explanations were not evaluated.
values.label: No

values.summary: Evaluation using quantitative proxy metrics.
values.label: Functionally-grounded

values.summary: Evaluation involving user studies with laypeople on simplified tasks.
values.label: Human-grounded

values.summary: Evaluation via anecdotal evidence as defined by Nauta et al. [2] ("showing individual, convincing examples that pass the first test of having face-validity").
values.label: Anecdotal evidence

dimensions.label: Co-12 Properties
dimensions.description: The Co-12 properties evaluated in a study as defined by Nauta et al. [2].

values.summary: Describes how faithful the explanation is w.r.t. the black box.
values.label: Correctness

values.summary: Describes how much of the black box behavior is described in the explanation.
values.label: Completeness

values.summary: Describes how deterministic and implementation-invariant the explanation method is.
values.label: Consistency

values.summary: Describes how continuous and generalizable the explanation function is.
values.label: Continuity

values.summary: Describes how discriminative the explanation is w.r.t. other events or targets.
values.label: Contrastivity

values.summary: Describes how complex the (interactions of) features in the explanation are.
values.label: Covariate complexity

values.summary: Describes the size of the explanation.
values.label: Compactness

values.summary: Describes the presentation format and organization of the explanation.
values.label: Composition

values.summary: Describes the presence and accuracy of probability information in the explanation.
values.label: Confidence

values.summary: Describes how relevant the explanation is to the user and their needs.
values.label: Context

values.summary: Describes how accordant the explanation is with prior knowledge and beliefs.
values.label: Coherence

values.summary: Describes how interactive or controllable an explanation is for a user.
values.label: Controllability

dimensions.label: Benchmarked
dimensions.description: Describes whether the XUQ method was compared against other methods.

values.summary: The method was benchmarked against other approaches.
values.label: Yes

values.summary: The method was not benchmarked.
values.label: No
